findings.title: Xen Security Advisory XSA-523 v2: arbitrary read/write via grant copy (CVE-2026-102703, CVE-2026-102704)
findings.summary_md: The Xen Project publicly released XSA-523 version 2 on 2026-11-03 at 12:00 UTC, disclosing two grant-copy validation flaws that let a malicious guest read and write arbitrary memory of other domains, including Dom0. All Xen versions from 4.6 onward are vulnerable and 4.5 and earlier are not; the advisory states there is no known mitigation. The issue was discovered by Anthropic using Claude, validated by Stephan Lipp of Ada Logics, and independently reported by the CodeAnt AI Security Research Team. Attached patches cover xen-unstable through 4.19.x and 4.18.x through 4.17.x.

findings.title: oss-sec: Xen Security Advisory 523 v2 (CVE-2026-102703, CVE-2026-102704) - arbitrary read/write via grant copy
findings.summary_md: The oss-security mailing list carried the signed Xen advisory text on 2026-11-03 at 12:00:20 UTC, mirroring XSA-523 v2 and its CVE assignments. It restates the impact as arbitrary memory read and write across domains including Dom0, the affected range of Xen 4.6 and later, and the absence of any mitigation. The message also lists the patch filenames and SHA-256 checksums for the two patch sets.

findings.title: QSB-121: Arbitrary read/write via grant copy (XSA-523)
findings.summary_md: The Qubes Security Team published QSB-121 on 2026-11-03 confirming that all supported Qubes OS releases and configurations are affected, with a malicious qube able to read and write other qubes' memory including dom0. The fix ships as Xen packages version 4.19.6-3 for Qubes 4.3 dom0 via the security-testing repository, requiring a dom0 restart afterward. Anti Evil Maid users must reseal their passphrase because PCR18 and PCR19 change with the new Xen binaries.

findings.title: VSA-2026-055: arbitrary read/write via grant copy (CVE-2026-102703, CVE-2026-102704 / XSA-523)
findings.summary_md: Vates rated the issue Critical for XCP-ng and published VSA-2026-055 on 2026-11-03 with no known mitigation. XCP-ng 8.3 is affected and the fix ships as xen-4.17.7-4.2.xcpng8.3 packages released the same day. The advisory repeats the Xen Project's credit to Anthropic using Claude, validation by Stephan Lipp of Ada Logics, and the independent report from the CodeAnt AI Security Research Team.

findings.title: Xen Hypervisor Guest Escape (CVE-2026-102703, CVE-2026-102704)
findings.summary_md: Ostorlab published a deep dive on 2026-11-04 at 10:00 UTC tracing the root cause to commit d28f42f2703e, which introduced the deferred-release grant-copy cache in Xen 4.6.0 and matches the advisory's vulnerable range. The post notes that no Xen release tarball carried the XSA-523 patches as of 2026-11-04 and that branches 4.6 through 4.16 receive no upstream patch because they are end of life. It also records that no exploitation was known and neither CVE was in the CISA KEV catalog as of that date.
